title: Decline of the brass bands, long walks and union pay
summary: The brass bands faded as players died or left; he recalls walking ten miles for a dollar, all-night dances, and pay changing once the union came.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Um... Well, they used to like that, but they cut it out after the band, whatever, all the distance, and had many brass bands. And when all the fellas that used to play, they all died, some left here, and... Wasn't much here, so we didn't want to get a dollar to walk about, what, 10 miles. She wasn't walking all right. Well, what, 10 miles for a dollar. 10 miles for a dollar. That's right. She all night started dancing. What time did we start dancing? Seven o'clock or eight o'clock? Seven o'clock. Seven o'clock. Seven o'clock. Seven o'clock. Eight o'clock. Well, they played at four o'clock. Four o'clock in the morning. Seven o'clock in the morning. Seven o'clock in the morning. Sometimes a man would make enough money to pay you. They don't pay the four hours, no. Yeah, the four hours. You get about fifteen, twenty dollars or something. Well, you see, after it started getting union fee. Yeah. It's changing all that dollars. Change, yeah. It's changing. Yeah, you know. What, you used to kill? You don't know Mr. Marshall? Yeah, I told him I'll carry around.
We don't go by there in a while.
Yeah, I told him I'll carry around over there.
